summary: Backend-only regression to verify the PUT /api/payments/{id} bug fix in /app/backend/server.py (new handler at line 382). Ran TestPutPayment class first (2/2 passed) then full backend suite (60/60 passed). PUT with valid id returns updated fields without _id; PUT with non-existent id returns HTTP 404 (no longer 405). Other PUT handlers (suppliers/bills/sales) and all prior features unaffected.

minor.issue: Handler performs update_one() before the 404 existence check. On a missing id the update is a no-op so behavior is correct today, but consider checking existence first (or using result.matched_count) to avoid the wasted write and to be consistent with other PUT handlers.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py PUT /payments/{pid}: minor - reorder so existence is checked before update, or assert matched_count > 0, to align with other PUT handlers.
seed_data_creation: None. Existing tests create/cleanup their own fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: PUT /api/payments/{pid} handler exists at server.py:382. All 60 backend tests currently pass. No frontend tests were run this iteration.
rca_of_issue: Root cause of prior 405: no PUT route was registered for /payments/{pid}; FastAPI fell through to the collection-level route or returned 405. Fix: added @api_router.put('/payments/{pid}') update_payment handler that upserts the PaymentCreate body and returns the persisted document (without _id) or raises 404. Verified via pytest: TestPutPayment.test_update_payment and test_update_payment_404 both pass.
